To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the blue color displayed by the CuO4 chromophore in Han and Egyptian blue pigments arises from the red-shift of its x(2)- y(2) transition induced by a strong electrostatic field produced by the lattice.

The origin of the bright blue hue of Egyptian Blue (Ca-Cu-Si-O system) and Han Blue pigments (Ba-Cu-Si system) is due to the red-shift of a transition in the CuO(4) chromophore caused by the electrostatic field created from the surrounding lattice.

the unusual bright blue hue displayed by historical Egyptian and Han Blue pigments is not due to a change in the electronic configuration of the copper atom, nor to an unusual oxidation state, but to the presence of an electric field created by the lattice that red-shifts the absorption of the chromophore by 7100 cm-1.

the color of a pigment is not only determined by the chemical composition of the chromophore but also by the crystal structure where the chromophore is located.
